web_evidence.title: The Testaments — official Vintage/Penguin sample
web_evidence.note: A sustained publisher-authorized sample interleaves the Ardua Hall Holograph and Witness Testimony 369A; both Aunt Lydia and Agnes narrate their story-world experiences in first person.

web_evidence.title: American Nightmares: Dystopia in Twenty-First-Century US Fiction
web_evidence.note: The scholarly structural analysis states that Aunt Lydia, Agnes Jemima, and Daisy provide three first-person narratives as a holograph and two witness-testimony transcripts, followed by a symposium coda.

web_evidence.title: The Testaments: Key Facts
web_evidence.note: Explicitly identifies all three narrators and states that each speaks from her own perspective using first-person I; it also identifies the final historian section.

web_evidence.title: Review: The Testaments by Margaret Atwood
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly describes the novel as using multiple first-person narrators whose testaments function as primary historical sources.

web_evidence.title: Margaret Atwood: ‘For a long time we were moving away from Gilead. Then we started going back towards it’
web_evidence.note: The author interview identifies the three constitutive voices as Aunt Lydia's testament and the testimonies of Agnes and Daisy, corroborating the document-based narrator structure.

person_note: The diagnostic quotations repeatedly expose participating I/we narration, and the authorized sample independently confirms sustained first-person accounts by Aunt Lydia and Agnes. Whole-book scholarly and explicit reference evidence establishes that Daisy's third constitutive testimony is also first person. Thus the novel has three narrators but not multiple grammatical persons: under the methodology, multiple first-person narrators remain FIRST rather than ALTERNATING. Dialogue, generic you, and aphoristic material were not promoted to narrator evidence. The concluding historical symposium frames and evaluates the three documents but does not create a sustained third-person story strand. Remaining uncertainty is minimal and concerns only the sparse quote coverage of Daisy, resolved by the whole-book structural evidence.
